solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Caught judge leaving in a better mood — start to yell for mine

indicators.note: the judge goes out of the word, so J is removed
the start of a word is its first letter

blocks.clueFragment: judge leaving in a better mood
blocks.note: JOLLIER (in a better mood) with J (judge) taken out

explanation.surface: A judge is arrested and, in a better mood once off the bench, heads off shouting for a mine.
explanation.walkthrough: The judge is only the letter J, and it leaves JOLLIER rather than the courtroom. A colliery is a coal mine.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a colliery is a coal mine together with its surface buildings.

clue.text: Giant cuts introduced by Conservative Party maniac at last

indicators.note: takes the last letter of each word before it
the cuts come after the letters that introduce them

blocks.note: last letters of partY and maniaC

explanation.surface: A political story: a Conservative Party maniac finally unveils huge cuts.
explanation.walkthrough: "Giant" reads as an adjective for the cuts, but it is the noun: the one-eyed giant of Greek myth.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cyclops is the one-eyed giant of Greek myth.

clue.text: Fabric worn by Father on church steps

indicators.note: the fabric goes around Father, as clothes go around a wearer
in a down clue, the first part sits on top of the next

explanation.surface: A priest in his linen vestments stands on the church steps.
explanation.walkthrough: "Father" suggests a priest in vestments on the church steps, but the steps are dance steps.
explanation.definitionFit: A line dance is a set sequence of steps danced in rows.

clue.text: Japanese art outlaw’s hidden in furniture shop

indicators.note: the outlaw's letters are put inside the shop's name

explanation.surface: A fugitive hides out in a furniture store, like a scene from a caper film.
explanation.walkthrough: "Outlaw" looks like a criminal but is the verb: to outlaw is to BAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by category: formal flower arranging is one of Japan's traditional arts.

clue.text: Grab ice, running for Costa’s location

indicators.note: letters that are running are in motion, so rearranged

explanation.surface: A hurried order in a Costa coffee shop: grab some ice and run.
explanation.walkthrough: Costa is a UK coffee-shop chain, but here it is the Latin for a rib, so its location is the ribcage.
explanation.definitionFit: Costa is Latin (and anatomy's term) for a rib, and ribs sit in the ribcage.

clue.text: Reason test is without beginning or end

indicators.note: strip the first and last letters

blocks.note: the MOT is the UK's annual roadworthiness test for cars
LIVES (is, exists) loses L and S

explanation.surface: A logician complains that a test is endless.
explanation.walkthrough: "Is" must become LIVES, as in 'it lives' meaning 'it exists', before it loses its ends.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the reason behind an action is what drives it.

clue.text: Ship always following line taken by cutter

indicators.note: the letters are taken into the cutter

explanation.surface: A naval scene: a ship forever trailing a line behind a cutter, which is also a small boat.
explanation.walkthrough: A cutter is a kind of sailing boat, which suits the ship, but here it is a lawnmower.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mayflower carried the Pilgrims to America in 1620.

clue.text: Speaker rather sentimental about closure of parliament on reflection

indicators.note: the closing letter of parliament
a reflection shows things back to front

explanation.surface: A politician speaks with rather sentimental regret about parliament shutting down.
explanation.walkthrough: The Speaker of the House is the obvious reading, but the speaker is a loudspeaker. Only the last two pieces turn round; the sentimental part stays as it is.
explanation.definitionFit: A tweeter is a small loudspeaker for the high notes.

clue.text: Surrounded by thieves, I clean small cell

indicators.note: the answer sits surrounded by the letters of the words around it

blocks.note: the letters run from the last three of thieves, through I, into the first three of clean

explanation.surface: A prisoner in a small cell among thieves insists they are going straight.
explanation.walkthrough: The prison cell of the surface is a biological one, and the thieves only surround the letters: thie(VES I CLE)an.
explanation.definitionFit: A vesicle is a small sac or cell-like cavity in the body.

clue.text: Is US hospital department unable to purchase right parts for stand?

blocks.note: ER = emergency room, the American casualty department

explanation.surface: A question about a US emergency room that cannot afford spare parts for a stand.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the clue as 'the department is unable', so the unable part comes first. A canterbury is a low stand with divisions for sheet music or magazines.
explanation.definitionFit: A canterbury is a small open-topped stand for music or papers.

clue.text: Relaxation barely stops

indicators.note: made bare, stripped of its outer letters

blocks.note: CEASES (stops) stripped of C and S

explanation.surface: Relaxation barely stops before work begins again.
explanation.walkthrough: "Barely" reads as 'hardly', but here it means stripping CEASES bare of its outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Ease is freedom from effort or strain: relaxation.

clue.text: Poor actor once active in group of players

blocks.note: a ham is an overacting performer

explanation.surface: A washed-up actor who was once energetic joins a theatre company.
explanation.walkthrough: "Group of players" suggests actors, but it is a football team: Oldham Athletic is an English club from near Manchester. 'Once poor actor' gives OLD HAM.
explanation.definitionFit: Oldham Athletic is an English professional football club, a group of players.

clue.text: City protected housing worker

indicators.note: the protected word houses the worker inside it

explanation.surface: A city provides protected housing for its workers.
explanation.walkthrough: "Housing" looks like accommodation but is the container instruction. Santa Fe is the capital of New Mexico.
explanation.definitionFit: Santa Fe is the capital city of New Mexico.

clue.text: Order member of Mensa, extremely reclusive, to mingle

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its outer letters
letters that mingle move among one another like guests at a party, so they end up in a new order

explanation.surface: A shy member of the high-IQ society Mensa is urged to socialise.
explanation.walkthrough: "Member of Mensa" looks like the definition, but the definition is "Order member", and "of Mensa" is anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Freemasonry is a fraternal order, so each of its members fits the definition directly.

clue.text: Stunted government department with Democrat’s backing

indicators.note: the whole string goes backwards

blocks.note: DEFRA = the UK Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

explanation.surface: A government department's work is held back even with a Democrat's support.
explanation.walkthrough: "Backing" reads as support, but it reverses DEFRA+W+D.
explanation.definitionFit: Dwarfed means stunted, kept small in growth.

clue.text: Denounce male unfit to work

indicators.note: the letters are worked into a new shape

explanation.surface: Someone condemns a man who is not fit to work.
explanation.walkthrough: "Unfit to work" reads as a medical note; "to work" alone is the anagram instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym with extra heat: fulminating is condemning in thunderous, furious terms.

clue.text: With difficulty, got wife then felt bitter about losing space

indicators.note: the word loses the letters for space

blocks.note: RESENTED loses EN, the printer's space

explanation.surface: Someone finally married, then resented feeling cramped.
explanation.walkthrough: An en is a printer's space half the width of an em, so 'space' can stand for EN.
explanation.definitionFit: Wrested means got something with effort, by pulling it away.

clue.text: Boring European finishes river trip, having spent grand

indicators.note: European comes at the end
the grand is used up, so G goes

explanation.surface: A dull European ends a pricey river cruise, a thousand pounds poorer.
explanation.walkthrough: "Boring" looks like a description of the European, but it is the definition. A grand is a thousand pounds, abbreviated G.
explanation.definitionFit: Routine can mean dull and ordinary, as in a routine job.

clue.text: Civil case rule shortly to be reformed

indicators.note: the word is cut short by one letter
the letters are formed again in a new order

explanation.surface: A lawyer says the rule in a civil case will soon be reformed.
explanation.walkthrough: "Civil case" is a legal phrase in the surface; only "Civil" is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Secular means not religious, as a civil wedding is.

clue.text: Dull young woman turned flapper

indicators.note: something turned round faces the other way, so the young woman's letters now read backwards

explanation.surface: A dull young woman reinvents herself as a 1920s flapper.
explanation.walkthrough: A flapper was a lively young woman of the 1920s, which fits the surface, but here it is anything that flaps its wings: a goose.
explanation.definitionFit: The greylag is a wild goose, and geese flap.

clue.text: Diary entry packed with fuss over London’s top primatologist

indicators.note: the diary entry is filled with the next letters
the fuss is turned over, back to front
the top of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: a goal is an aim you might write down in a diary
a do = a fuss, a to-do

explanation.surface: A gossipy diary item about a scientist making a fuss in London.
explanation.walkthrough: Jane Goodall is the British scientist famous for her decades studying chimpanzees in Tanzania.
explanation.definitionFit: Jane Goodall is the world's best-known primatologist.

clue.text: Showed cycling gadget with new lining

indicators.note: the first letter goes round to the end

blocks.note: DEVICE with its D moved from front to back

explanation.surface: Someone showed off a new gadget for their bicycle.
explanation.walkthrough: "Cycling gadget" reads as bike kit; "cycling" is the instruction to move DEVICE's first letter to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To evince is to show or reveal a feeling or quality.

clue.text: Before Republican elected, censor a former high-flying Russian

indicators.note: the censor and a come before the rest

explanation.surface: A Cold War story: before a Republican wins office, a Russian defector is silenced.
explanation.walkthrough: Yuri Gagarin became the first human in space in 1961, which makes him high-flying in the literal sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Yuri Gagarin, the Soviet cosmonaut, flew higher than anyone before him.

clue.text: Stubborn commander invades showing little likelihood of success

indicators.note: the commander invades the other word, going inside it

explanation.surface: A stubborn military commander launches an invasion that looks doomed.
explanation.walkthrough: The army story is surface; the commander goes inside the word for unlikely to succeed, just after its negative prefix.
explanation.definitionFit: Uncompromising means refusing to give way: stubborn.

clue.text: Source of pretty bad medicine

indicators.note: a word's source is where it begins, its first letter

blocks.note: ill = bad, as in ill effects

explanation.surface: A remark that some medicine is the source of pretty bad side effects.
explanation.walkthrough: "Pretty bad" reads as 'quite bad', but "pretty" only lends its P.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a small tablet is one of the forms medicine comes in.

clue.text: Shock after fringes of some key African party carried seat

indicators.note: the shock comes after the other pieces
the fringes of a word are its outer letters

blocks.note: the African National Congress, South Africa's ruling party

explanation.surface: An African political party wins a key seat, to everyone's shock.
explanation.walkthrough: "Seat" suggests a parliamentary seat; it is a chair carried on poles. "Shock" is not surprise but a mop of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A sedan chair is an enclosed seat carried on poles by two bearers.

clue.text: Article managed to move hearts in capital

blocks.note: ran = managed, as in ran a business

explanation.surface: A newspaper article managed to move readers' hearts in the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: "Move hearts" sounds emotional; it is an order to shift the H at the heart of THE one place along.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Iran's seat of government is one of the world's capital cities.

clue.text: Shift over when prodded by large stick

explanation.surface: Someone on a bench is poked with a large stick until they shift over.
explanation.walkthrough: "Large stick" looks like the definition, but "large" gives the L, and the definition is "stick" alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a thick, heavy club used as a weapon is a kind of stick.
